newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal arrests four in Japanese monk murder case.
newsitem.headline: Nepal arrests four in Japanese monk murder case.

text.p: Nepali police have arrested four of six people suspected of killing a Japanese monk at Lumbini, the birth place of Lord Buddha, the kingdom's police chief said on Tuesday.
Police chief Dhurba Bahadur Pradhan said police were "very close" to arresting the remaining two, one of whom is believed to be the actual killer.
The monk, Yonataka Nawatame, was shot dead on July 3 by six masked gunmen at Lumbini, 350 km (220 miles) west of Kathmandu, and near the Indian border.

The Himalaya Times newspaper said three people were arrested in New Delhi and were flown into Kathmandu on Monday night. Another was detained in the Nepali capital. Pradhan said all six suspects were Nepali.
Lord Buddha was born a prince in Lumbini. He received enlightenment at Gaya in the eastern Indian state of Bihar, which borders Nepal.

Foreign religious institutions are building monasteries and shrines in Lumbini as part of an international drive to develop the site. Nawatame was supervising the construction of a peace pagoda, or temple tower, being built by a Japanese religious organisation, Nipponzan Myohoji.
Police said money was the motive for the murder.
Pradhan said a priest at the Mayadevi temple in Lumbini was originally the killers' target but they attacked the Japanese monk instead, thinking he had more money.
The killers asked for money and shot the monk after he refused, police said.
The murder has sparked strong protests in the Nepali parliament as well as from Buddhist religious organisations calling for tighter security for monks at Lumbini.
